From the literal side, when God dwells in their midst they are filled with good days and peace dwells in them; death does not surprise them in their youth, but they live to old age, full of health, as they go down to the marketplaces of the city to buy what they need, each holding his staff in his hand. From the symbolic side, the marketplaces of Jerusalem in which the elders, men and women, sit are the overflow of wisdom that flows like a river that makes glad the city of God (Ps 46:4); all can go down to it to drink from it, or enter the marketplaces to acquire it. As the wise man says: "Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets" (Prov 1:20). This wisdom is "the Person of the Lord Christ," who came down from heaven and presented Himself to us as a servant; all can acquire Him within and enjoy Him; He of whom the bride says: "By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not. I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth" (Song 3:1-2). As her heart burns with longing for her Bridegroom, she seeks "Wisdom Himself" and does not find Him beside her, so she rises through repentance from her bed and enters the Church, "the holy city," and goes about in its marketplaces and streets, and finds Him revealed within it, offering Himself to whoever seeks Him.

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Second: "And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof" [5]. The presence of boys and girls also in the marketplaces, playing, indicates the tranquility that prevailed over all and the absence of war that takes joy away from old and young. As Isaiah the prophet described the messianic age: "And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old" (Isa 65:19-20).

Along with the elders there are also children playing in the marketplaces; these are the company of the simple who have attained to "childhood" so as to live in the Lord without care, as if the marketplaces of the Church include the wisdom of the elders together with the simplicity of children, as the Lord said to His disciples: "Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves" (Mt 10:16). And as St. Jerome says: [Be simple as a dove so that you set a snare for no one, and be wise (skilful) as a serpent so that you allow no one to set a snare before you].

St. Didymus the Blind offers us a wonderful interpretation of these simple children who play in the marketplaces of the Church, that is, the holy city: [There are also little girls and boys who have begun to play a game worthy of praise, which David played, the man whose heart was according to the Lord (Acts 13:22; 1 Sam 13:14), fulfilling the will of Him who chose him, declaring with sure confidence: "I played before the LORD" (2 Sam 6:21). We can say that the children who play in the public places (the marketplaces) of the glorious city of the Lord are people who were consecrated to the Lord from their childhood, so that with purity and deep dignity they have been joined to holy speech that is blameless (Tit 2:7-8)].

In our commentary on the Book of Exodus we saw that the boys signify the soul and the girls the body; so when a person is sanctified in his entirety he brings forth fruits for the soul and the body together. There is no longer conflict between them, but they work together by the Holy Spirit, and the fruits come as boys and girls playing together in the marketplaces of the holy city with a glorious joy that cannot be uttered.

Finally, the marketplaces of the city have included the elders together with the old women, and the boys with the girls, that is, men with women, and the old with the young... As St. Didymus the Blind says: [All have become one choir singing one hymn with one heart, as it is written in the Psalm: "Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children: let them praise the name of the LORD" (Ps 148:12-13). As she cares for the wise elders, she does not neglect the wise old women who play their role in the Church. And as the Church rejoices in the wisdom of the elders, she is also glad in the victory of the young men, for the Apostle says: "I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one" (1 Jn 2:12-14)].

This divine work in the life of all members of the Church seems impossible, for the prophet says: "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the LORD of hosts?!" [6]. If the enemy had utterly destroyed Jerusalem, so that in the eyes of all it was impossible for joy to return to her, yet not in God's eyes, for "with God all things are possible" (Mt 19:26)... He restores to her her glory and her joy by His dwelling in her!

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Third: "Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness" [7-8].

The new Jerusalem does not include one choir of elders and old women and boys and girls, but one people of the Lord from the rising of the sun and its setting, for the door of salvation opens to all the nations and all become one in the Lord. This is the great blessing of God's dwelling among men and His abiding among us. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Thus saith the LORD of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country, not only the people of the circumcision but the people from all the nations who believe in the Lord who is proclaimed in the Gospel. In ancient times the people in truth were of one nation, of the Hebrews... according to the testimony of Moses: "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance" (Deut 32:8-9)... As it was said: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" (Isa 11:10; Rom 15:12)... "Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people" (Deut 32:43). So this people is no longer the people of the Hebrews alone, but with them are those who worship the Lord and serve Him, as the Psalm prophesied: "All nations shall serve him" (Ps 72:11), and in another text: "All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name" (Ps 86:9), and also: "All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee. For the kingdom is the LORD's: and he is the governor among the nations" (Ps 22:27-28)... And the Gospel proclaims the union of men from every country by recording the words of the Savior: "Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob" (Mt 8:11). This call is addressed to all parts of the world. To this may be added what was said: "The God of gods, the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof" (Ps 50:1)... When did the God of gods speak and call the earth from the east to the west? When He left the people of the circumcision because they denied the Savior, the King of kings, by saying: "We have no king but Caesar" (Jn 19:15), "His blood be on us, and on our children" (Mt 27:25). So by their crucifying the Lord Christ they fell and the worship of the letter came to an end, and the Lord was able to say to them: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen" (Mal 1:10-11)...].

Thus God restores humanity from the east and the west to be a people for Him in truth and righteousness. And what we say about humanity we say about the individual: God restores him from every blow on the right (from the east) and every blow on the left (from the west), that is, from falling under open sins and from self-righteousness, so that he may belong wholly to God, enjoying truth and righteousness in Christ Jesus.

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Fourth: As the people of God gather from all the nations with one heart, it has the strengthened, strong hands that are able through the Lord to build the temple: "Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built" [9]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord Almighty commands that the hands consecrated to Him be strong... by translating the spiritual teachings into real work, so that work is joined to word; so that the hearers of the Law are not mere hearers, but turn hearing into fruit in their works].

If we have heard from the mouths of the prophets about the founding of the house of the LORD of hosts, that is, about the divine Incarnation, for the Lord Himself calls His body a temple, then this Incarnation gives strength to our hands to work by it, so that the divine commandment is transformed in our lives into a practical life lived out. God raised up this body, as it is said: "Wisdom hath builded her house" (Prov 9:1), so that God became dwelling in our midst and gives us His heavenly resources to work for the sake of His Kingdom. And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [How should the hands of those who hear the words of the prophets not be strong, when there was born of the Virgin the One who is fit to be called "God with us" (Isa 7:14)?! In truth, when God is with us our hands are strong and we can sing with a joyful voice: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge" (Ps 45:11-12)... He gives us a strength that transcends nature!].

Therefore let our hands be strengthened for work, and let the words of God in us be turned into life, since the Word built Himself a house by His Incarnation, giving us power to work. He has also made of us holy living stones for the building of His holy temple, for He says: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we (I and my Father) will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23). He makes us ourselves a dwelling for Him, or a holy temple upon which the cornerstone stands, as the Apostle says: "And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone..." (Eph 2:20)].

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Fifth: Our meeting with the incarnate God, and His dwelling in our midst, did not only strengthen the hands with His divine resources working in us, but also cut off the spirit of despair within us and set our depths aflame with hope. For work needs not only strong hands and striving and perseverance but also a spirit full of hope in the Lord; therefore He says: "For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour" [10]. Affliction surrounded them (Hag 1:6, 9, 11; 2:16-19), which made man like the beast, without value, so that even if the two did something it was without profit and they did not deserve a wage! Jerusalem was desolate like a wilderness and ruled by strangers, so every effort a man made availed nothing. The toil of man, like that of the beast, in his going in or coming out became without profit, which turned their life into hell, so each one went out resisting his brother for no cause; in other words, instead of each working with his brother for the building of the house of God, each felt humiliation, total loss and inner emptiness, and so turned to resisting his brothers and troubling them.

From the spiritual side, a person without his meeting with his Savior, who established His holy temple, is like the beast: he works without understanding or wisdom, and so does not deserve a wage. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Scripture rebukes those who are without mind, who are in folly, saying: "Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding" (Ps 83:9). Truly, how can there be a wage for people who do everything without understanding or reason?!].

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: This is a bitter picture of humanity apart from the work of God: it goes out to work and comes in to reckoning and finds itself in emptiness, without fruit, and not deserving reward, since each one is occupied with resisting his brother, as the Psalm says: "They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips" (Ps 12:3), and as was said by Jeremiah the prophet: "Every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders. And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity" (Jer 9:4-5). But under the New Covenant Jerusalem stands on true peace and brings increasing fruits, so the toil of man and beast is no longer without wage as it was formerly. He says: "But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the LORD of hosts. But the seed of peace; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things: [11-12]. What a joyful picture after man was working without reason like the beast, so that he had no wage, as the soul (man) loses its fruit as the body (the beast) loses its sanctity, and each resists the other; now that the Lord dwells in him, not only does his soul enjoy the wage but his body also, and there is spiritual accord between them and he has surpassing spiritual fruit, and the earth works on his behalf as heaven does, in the Lord. As the Lord returns to him and dwells within him and establishes His kingdom in his heart, the seed of peace appears, which the Father Himself plants by His Holy Spirit, and the fruits of the Holy Spirit appear as the fruits of the true vine, and the earth (the body) gives its increase as the body bears a special sanctity and becomes instruments of righteousness for God, and heaven (the soul) gives its dew, as the grace of the Holy Spirit fills it... All these God gives to the soul that receives Him in it.

St. Didymus the Blind says: [This glorious reform was fulfilled in the spiritual sense when He came who said: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised" (Lk 4:18)... It is written: "In his days shall the righteous shine forth, and abundance of peace; his peace shall know no barriers; it shall not be for one nation but for the company of the nations." The whole earth that is subject to Him who said to His disciples and to those who desire to serve Him: "My peace I give unto you" (Jn 14:27) enjoys a great calm that is established in it, and the vine gives its fruit and the earth its increase and heaven its dew. The vine that gives its fruit is the spiritual contemplations in the truth... and the earth gives its increase, as the seed that Jesus cast into it bears thirty and sixty and a hundred (Mt 13:8, 23)... The earth presents its increase to him who sows it with tears and with sweat and sorrow, so he reaps it with joy (Ps 125:5)... "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him" (Ps 126:5). This abundant harvest is spiritual and concerns the divine word, as Hosea the prophet commanded: "Sow to yourselves in righteousness; reap according to goodness; plow for yourselves a plowing, for it is a time to seek the Lord until He come and teach you righteousness" (Hos 10:12)... As for heaven giving its dew, we shall understand the dew when we know the heaven that gives it. Heaven is no doubt none other than he who bears the image of the heavenly man (1 Cor 15:49), whose homeland is in heaven (Phil 3:20). For it was said of those who show forth the heavenly image of the Savior: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Ps 18:1), and it was said of them in the great song in the Book of Deuteronomy: "Rejoice, O ye heavens, with him" (Deut 32:43), that is, rejoice with the Savior. How should they not rejoice and exult with Him when they have been formed in His image, as the Apostle says: "to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Rom 8:29), and also "we shall put on the image of the heavenly" (1 Cor 15:49)?! It is fitting for us to say that by their union in one heaven they give a heavenly dew, but each one gives his own dew, imitating Moses who said: "My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew" (Deut 32:2)].

Sixth: As the believer, by God's dwelling in his heart, comes to have these divine blessings, he becomes a heaven that gives its dew, for he is no longer a curse to others nor to himself, but is a blessing... This is what we speak of in the commentary on the end of this chapter [20-23].

entries.section: 3. Reminding them of the commandment:

paragraphs.text: 16 These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: 17 And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD.

Amid these blessings that come upon their lives by the Lord's dwelling in them, which seem as if impossible [9], He urges them to hold fast to the divine commandment so that they do not fall under His wrath like their fathers. "These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: and let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD" [16-17].

Now that He is rebuilding the temple and renewing Jerusalem, His holy city, He wanted this work to be founded on truth joined to righteousness, or in other words to be based on practical truth in the lives of His children. And here we notice the following in these commandments of His:

First: He begins with our relationship with our brethren in the Lord, such as speaking with our brethren in truth, and judging with justice and peace, etc... and ends with a commandment concerning our relationship with Him, "a false oath," as if God wants our inner Jerusalem to be founded on true practical love with our brethren, yet in the Lord.

Second: He begins by speaking of "truth"; this is the foundation of true building. What is this truth with which we speak to our neighbors and by which we judge but the manifestation of the "Lord Christ" Himself in our speech as in our conduct, for He declared of Himself that He is "the truth." This truth is not preached by word only but is proclaimed with power through practical conduct in the lives of the shepherds as of the flock.

St. Didymus the Blind sees that the Lord begins His speech concerning the spiritual leaders, who must proclaim "the truth" not by theoretical intellectual knowledge alone but through a virtuous life and practical conduct. Among his words in commenting on this divine statement: [It is fitting for us to hear the words of Jesus and practice them, as He Himself declared: "Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man" (Mt 7:24)].

[Let our deeds declare the spiritual teachings that we present; thus a man becomes "a workman that needeth not to be ashamed" (2 Tim 2:15). With this thought the Apostle writes to his disciple to keep purity, gravity, sincerity and sound speech that cannot be condemned (Tit 2:7-8). What is sound speech that cannot be condemned but practicing what we enjoin on others, and our pure fidelity to what we hold out to others concerning the faith?!].

Thus the Fathers of the Church affirmed the necessity of proclaiming the truth by practical life and its manifestation in daily conduct. Among the words of St. John Chrysostom: [He who governs others must be more radiant than any shining star; his life must be without blemish; all look to him and see in his life a model for themselves].

Third: He continues His speech, saying: "execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates"... If "truth" is the foundation on which the new city is built, then it is fitting that truth be mixed with peace. Heavenly truth opens the heart with love so that it is wide enough to bear with others, being at peace, if possible, with all men.

St. Didymus the Blind comments on His saying "in your gates," saying that the courts of justice founded on truth mixed with peace are at the gates, to sort those entering the city from those who are barred from it. It is as though peace does not mean flattery at the expense of truth or leniency toward evil, but while the heart is widened with love, nothing defiled or abominable must enter the holy city!
Let us love all and open our hearts to peace with all, but let us not open our inner gates to evil and sin out of courtesy to others!

Fourth: "let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour," meaning the inner forgetting of every wrong a neighbor has done to us, or not thinking ill of his actions. Joseph the Righteous presents to us a living example of this virtue; in his composure he realizes what his brothers did to him, but his heart sees beyond his brothers' actions: the hand of God working for his salvation and theirs; therefore with a wide heart he said to them: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Gen 45:5) "But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive" (Gen 50:20).

When a man realizes the divine purposes his soul rests greatly in everything, and his heart is widened with peace for everyone, even for his opponents, so he does not resist evil with evil but with good and with love.
Fifth: Finally He asks them not to love a false oath, which the Lord hates, since He commanded us: "Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain" (Ex 20:7).

entries.section: 4. The fasts turn into feasts:

paragraphs.text: 18 And the word of the LORD of hosts came unto me, saying, 19 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace.

"The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace" [18-19].

Their past life had been marked by fasting with mourning because of the chastenings that came upon them for their sins; and now that the Lord dwells in their midst and declares His dwelling in them, He turns their hearts to joy and their life to an unceasing feast. So also the true Christian in the midst of his fasts and sufferings, as he realizes the indwelling of God in him, inner joy does not cease from him and the feast does not stop in his life.

In the previous chapter we spoke about fasting as not merely abstaining from food but stopping from evil together with enjoying the Lord Christ, the bread of life. This concerns spiritual fasting; as for the feast, St. Athanasius the Apostolic says: [Jesus Christ, who is the way and the door and everything for us, is also "our feast," as the blessed Paul says: "For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us" (1 Cor 5:7)]. And as fasting is not merely abstaining from foods, so the feast is not eating and drinking but a joyful life in the Lord. Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [Let us not keep the feast in an earthly manner but as those who keep a feast in heaven with the angels... Let us rejoice not in ourselves but in the Lord, so that we may be with the saints]. [Let us not stop at merely performing the rites of the feast but prepare to draw near to the divine Lamb and touch the heavenly food].

entries.section: 5. Their dwelling a blessing for the nations:

paragraphs.text: 20 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; It shall yet come to pass, that there shall come people, and the inhabitants of many cities: 21 And the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to pray before the LORD, and to seek the LORD of hosts: I will go also. 22 Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the LORD. 23 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you."

God does not accept half measures: either one is a curse to himself as to others, or a blessing to himself as to his brethren, for He says: "And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing" [13]. And here He explains to them how they will be a blessing, saying: "Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the LORD... In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you" [22-23].

First: When God's wrath came upon them and the captivity took place, they became a curse among the nations; and the sign of this curse is the ruin of Jerusalem even in the days of the feast, as Jeremiah says lamenting Zion: "The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn feasts: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh" (Lam 1:4). And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [How should the ways of Zion not mourn, when no one comes to her and there is none to hasten in going up to Jerusalem to celebrate the feast and to assemble there...?!]. But now that she has turned from curse to blessing she has drawn many peoples to her so that they may enjoy the feast and rejoice in the Lord. Zechariah the prophet says: "Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem." And since Jerusalem means "vision of peace," the sign of blessing is the drawing of many to enjoy this spiritual vision of reconciliation on the Cross and obtaining peace with God.

Second: St. Didymus the Blind comments on the saying: "I will go also." He says that the prophet, seeing crowds of peoples and nations coming from Jerusalem, had his heart set aflame with longing, and desired to be among those coming, declaring it by his saying: "I will go also." He also sees that the speaker here is the Savior, who declares His entrance into Jerusalem, leading these peoples in the spirit of victory, saying: "I have raised him up with victory, and I will make all his ways smooth; he shall build my city, and shall release my captives, not for price nor for reward, saith the LORD of hosts" (Isa 45:13). As He opens the door, the door of victory and triumph, and builds the inner holy city, and frees the soul from its captivity not by a material price or an earthly reward but by His precious blood, the peoples and nations seek the Lord and enter the new Jerusalem to entreat the Lord's favor, those of whom the Apostle said: "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven" (Heb 12:22-23).

Third: The Lord does not say that He blesses them but what is greater: "ye shall be a blessing"; through them the nations are blessed, and in Zephaniah He says that they become "a praise among all the peoples of the earth" (Zeph 3:20), and in Micah they become "as a dew from the LORD" (Mic 5:7). So he who carries the Lord in his heart carries a blessing for others, and is a song of joy by which their hearts rejoice in the Lord; they become like the heavenly dew that quenches the flame of the world's destructive fire!

Fourth: He concludes His speech about the blessing with the fact that ten men from all languages of the nations take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you. This is a picture of the bride who says in the Song: "Draw me, we will run after thee" (Song 1:4), for as she sets out toward her Bridegroom she carries with her ten persons whom she gains for the Lord by her holy life and her witness for the Lord. This from one side, and from another side we who were formerly of the Gentiles do not deny that we have received from them the Old Testament with what it contains of the Law and the prophecies as a way to the knowledge of salvation in Christ Jesus. We are indebted to them for receiving the faith in the Messiah the Savior.

St. Didymus the Blind sees that this Jew by whose skirt ten men from all the nations take hold is none other than the Lord Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah (Heb 7:14), as was said by Isaiah the prophet: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" (Isa 11:10). He is the object of expectation not of one nation but of all the nations.

As for the number ten, it signifies, in the opinion of St. Didymus the Blind, the believers who have become ten virgins (Mt 25:1), having five holy senses of the body and five holy inner senses. As for these, since the believers bear the name "Jesus Christ," the beginning of His name is the letter "Iota," which is equivalent to the number 10 in the Greek language.

entries.section: 1. The nations' revolt against Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: 1 The burden of the word of the LORD for Israel, saith the LORD, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him. 2 "Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, when they shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem. 3 And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it."

When the soul receives its Christ within it, the new Jerusalem becomes a member of the house of Judah, and in proportion to the graces it receives it meets resistance from the enemy (the nations), by God's permission, so that the evil of the wicked one may fill its cup and the Lord, the Giver of victory, may be revealed in His children. Through the enemy's harassment of God's children, the others become a cup of trembling to the first, and a burdensome stone to him, and a fire that burns him, as the prophet says: "Saith the LORD, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him, Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, when they shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem. And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it" [1-3].

The cup of trembling often signifies the wrath of God, when a man drinks it and loses consciousness and becomes like one in a state of reeling without balance, so that no one, not even one of his sons or daughters, is able to lead him or take him by the hand. This is as it is written in Isaiah: "Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out. There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she hath brought forth; neither is there any that taketh her by the hand of all the sons that she hath brought up" (Isa 51:17-18). And as it was said by Jeremiah: "Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it. And they shall drink, and be moved, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them" (Jer 25:15).

So when God wishes to give these peoples (as a symbol of the devil) the cup of His wrath to drink, that they may reel, He leaves them to stretch out their hands against Judah, and they fall under the wrath of God, the full measure of their own cup.
Once again God likens His children to the lifted stone, which the wicked carry in order to throw it down and shatter it, but behold, they are cut in pieces, or crushed, beneath it.

entries.section: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

paragraphs.text: 4 In that day, saith the LORD, I will smite every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah, and will smite every horse of the people with blindness. 5 And the governors of Judah shall say in their heart, The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength in the LORD of hosts their God. 6 In that day will I make the governors of Judah like a lamp of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire among the sheaves; and they shall devour all the people round about, on the right hand and on the left: and Jerusalem shall abide again in her own place, even in Jerusalem. 7 The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah. 8 In that day shall the LORD defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that stumbleth among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the LORD before them. 9 And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

"In that day, saith the LORD, I will smite every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah, and will smite every horse of the people with blindness" [4].

He smites the horse and its rider, who resists God's work in His children. The blow is astonishment, madness and blindness; that is, the enemy loses his peace, his balance and his insight, while the Lord opens His eyes upon the house of Judah, His Church, and becomes her leader and helper, and by Him He strikes the enemy with blindness, so that he is confused in his warfare and loses the battle.

St. Didymus the Blind sees that the horse here is the demon of error, falsehood and cunning, and its riders are those who promote these erroneous teachings, full of deceit; and that the blindness that strikes it is its deprivation of the Sun of Righteousness, who gives light. He also comments on God's opening His eyes upon the house of Judah, saying: [Afterward God opens His eyes upon the house of Judah, which is the church of the living God (1 Tim 3:15), where the Savior, who came from the tribe of Judah, reigns over those who have received wisdom from God, who say: "Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee" (Gen 49:8)... Upon the house of Judah the watchful God opens His eyes, that is, His luminous, watchful powers, and they enjoy enlightenment and grace, and each one prays, saying: "Look upon me and have mercy upon me" (Ps 25:16). This gift is enjoyed by all the righteous, for "the eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry" (Ps 34:15)].

entries.section: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

paragraphs.text: Not only is God the mystery of enlightenment to the house of Judah while He strikes the enemy with blindness, but He is also the mystery of strength to His people and the shattering of the devil, His enemy, for "the governors of Judah shall say in their heart, The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength in the LORD of hosts their God" [5].

entries.section: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

paragraphs.text: St. Didymus the Blind sees that if the Messiah is the spiritual King of His Church, then the disciples are the governors of Judah, who receive God as their God, a strength to them in their work of preaching. He gives them a divine, fiery power that burns up the sheaves of straw, for he says: "In that day will I make the governors of Judah like a lamp of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire among the sheaves; and they shall devour all the people round about, on the right hand and on the left: and Jerusalem shall abide again in her own place, even in Jerusalem. The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah" [6-7].

Although the new Judah has been called the little flock, it carries the fire of the Holy Spirit, which destroys the satanic blows from the right (self-righteousness) and from the left (impurities and lusts), and keeps the believer steadfast like Jerusalem, able to behold peace. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Being spiritually the governors of Judah, it is fitting for them to shatter, with their luminous, fiery speech, the deep fleshly will... It was said by Isaiah: "And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day; and shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body" (Isa 10:17-18), meaning that He destroys the corrupt intention as well as the corrupt deeds]. It is as though the fire of the Holy Spirit, who works in the spiritual man, burns the peoples round about, on the right hand and on the left; that is, He burns the evil intentions and deeds of the soul and the body together.
St. Didymus the Blind sees that the right hand and the left here signify extremes, for the Holy Spirit burns in the believer the spirit of stinginess as He burns the spirit of extravagance.

entries.section: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

paragraphs.text: It is wonderful that when God works by His fiery Spirit in the house of Judah, He begins with the tents of Judah [7] before saving the houses and palaces, that no one may have cause for boasting. He begins with the dwellers in tents, who are without protection, that they may not boast in their victory that they obtained salvation by their strength and their impregnable fortresses and their palaces and houses.

St. Didymus the Blind speaks of the tents of Judah that the Lord saves, saying: [These tents are the virtue of which it is said in Proverbs: "The tabernacle of the upright shall flourish" (Prov 14:11), and as the psalmist sings concerning the love that these tents inspire in him: "How amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!" (Ps 83:1). How should they not be loved, when they are full of those who keep their feasts, for the voices of joy and the works of grace cannot appear in any place other than the tents of the righteous (Ps 41:5; 17:15)?!].

He also sees in the tents of Judah a symbol of the mortal, humbled body that we wear, for when it enjoys God's salvation it puts on incorruption, glory and power, and is changed from a natural body to a spiritual body (1 Cor 15:42-44).

entries.section: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

paragraphs.text: As for the nullifying of the boasting of the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem against Judah, it points to the fall of the boasting of those who are wise in their own eyes, for the meek and the simple precede them, since God works with power in the one who feels his weakness: "He that stumbleth among them at that day (shall be) as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the LORD before them" [8]. That is, the weakest of them, the one who stumbles among them, will often be like David (2 Sam 17:8; 18:3), if God Himself is before him to support him. The mystery of victory is the appearance of God from the house of David, and as St. Didymus says: [The house of David here points to Mary, for the Lord comes incarnate from her. In that day, when the divine Incarnation is accomplished, the power of God is proclaimed in the new house of Judah, while the devil and his works perish and his authority over the believer is destroyed, for he says: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem" [9].

St. Didymus the Blind comments: [In that day draws near, when the night of ignorance and sin comes to an end, as the Apostle says: "The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light" (Rom 13:12). In that day He destroys all the peoples who bear a spirit of war against Jerusalem; He destroys those who are strangers to the truth and to the service of God, not by destroying men but by removing evil and ungodliness... Thus our Lord and Savior came seeking our lost race and delivering us by destroying all the peoples working against Jerusalem, that is, by destroying the causes of evil and war, forbidden deeds and heretical thoughts.

In brief we say that while the Lord is angry with those who resist, so that they reel from the cup of God's wrath, the believer himself is the cup [2]. And while God opens His eyes upon His children to support them and lead them in their spiritual warfare, behold, He strikes His enemies (the devil) with blindness [4]. And while God gives Himself to His children as a mystery of strength and a consuming fire, He makes the enemies (the sins) like sheaves of straw, and they are burned [6]. And while He supports the weak among His children who stumble, He destroys the enemy in his evil.

Thus the Lord supports His children, "the house of Judah," so that they enjoy His salvation through their reliance on Him, and as St. Serenus says: [Hear what the King (God) Himself says, approving the courageous men and summoning them to the spiritual warfare (against sin), saying: "Let the weak say, I am strong; let the sufferer be a wrestler" [(Joel 2:10-11) Septuagint]. Behold, you see that none but the suffering and the weak alone are those who fight in the divine battle, the weak who truly have the weakness of the centurion (Mt 8:9)... who said: "For when I am weak, then am I strong" (2 Cor 12:9), as it was said: "For my strength is made perfect in weakness" (2 Cor 12:9)].

entries.section: 3. The spirit of grace and supplications:

paragraphs.text: 10 "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. 11 In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon. 12 And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart; 13 The family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of Shimei apart, and their wives apart; 14 All the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart."

When the Lord reigns over the house of Judah, He pours out His Holy Spirit upon His Church to give her every grace and to support her in her striving until she crosses this world, and at the same time those who pierced the Lord with the spear of their sins fall under eternal judgment and are in great mourning.

"And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications" [10]. As St. Didymus the Blind says: [The spirit of grace and supplications is the Holy Spirit, the Giver of grace, who is given to us from the Father of mercies (2 Cor 3:3): "After the destruction of the nations (the devil and his works) Scripture adds that in that day to which it points He will pour upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of supplications, for He is the Father of supplications (2 Cor 1:3) and He has the Holy Spirit. Concerning this St. Paul writes: "Because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit which is given unto us" (Rom 5:5). And Solomon in the Book of Wisdom says: "And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above? For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee" (Wis 6:14-16). The Giver of the Holy Spirit says in Isaiah: "I will give thee my spirit" and also: "I have given him my spirit" (Isa 42)... as He says: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 3:1). And it is understood from the words of the Apostle that the spirit of grace is the Holy Spirit, for he says: "He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb 10:28-29)... Also the spirit of grace is the spirit of supplication (compassion), which is given from the Father of mercies (2 Cor 1:3)].

This is the fruit of the Cross, for He poured out upon the Church the Holy Spirit, the spirit of grace, who overflows with His divine graces and heavenly gifts, and the spirit of compassion, who supports and shows tenderness. But concerning those who reject salvation and aim the spear of sin, it is said of them: "And they shall look upon them whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon" [10-11].

St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Jews, the killers of Christ, suffered torments and were in mourning like one for whom a man dear to them has died, and they were filled with bitterness like one who has lost his firstborn son, for they perceived the wrath of God to the uttermost (1 Thess 2:16), so their homeland was taken from them and they were scattered over all the earth].
"There shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem"... perhaps it points to the Wailing Wall, when the Jews come from every corner of the world weeping over their condition and their dispersion!

Here he describes the mourning as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the plain of Megiddo, that place where the Egyptians killed King Josiah with their arrows, and Jeremiah the prophet and the singing men and singing women lamented him; and there had been no sorrow so general and so intense since Israel arose as a nation as there was when the royal chariot carried his body through the streets of Jerusalem to bury it.

He reveals the bitterness of this mourning by likening it to the mourning of parents over their only son. It touches the life of every family, indeed of every individual, so every family mourns apart, and the man mourns by himself and his wife by herself, for neither of them can bear to be comforted by the other, because of the terror of what they feel. Its cause is a collective offense directed against the Lord Christ who was pierced, for he says: "And they shall look upon them whom they have pierced."
Many of the Fathers comment on this phrase concerning the meeting of the wicked with the pierced Lord on the great day of the Lord. Among their words:
* They will learn that they shall know Him whom they pierced, and they will beat their breasts... Him whom they did not know before, because He came in the humility of His Incarnation.
* At the beginning they refused to recognize Him because of the humility of His Incarnation.

Tertullian * When He comes with His angels to judge (Mt 25:31), will those who pierced Him not see Him?! They will be confused, for the time will have passed because of their refusal of profitable repentance.
* He who was judged sits as Judge; He who stood before the judgment seat and was condemned for crimes falsely charged will judge the real crimes!

* He will come in a human form that the wicked will see... They look upon Him whom they pierced, for they gaze upon the body which they struck with the spear... And God remains (as far as they are concerned) hidden in the flesh, so they do not see the divinity (in its glory) after the judgment; rather, those on His right hand see it.

* The Son alone appears to the righteous and the wicked at the judgment in the same form that He had when He suffered and rose and ascended into heaven... But when the righteous go into eternal life they see Him as He is, and not as He came to judge the living and the dead, but He appears as a reward for the living!
St. Augustine The wicked mourn when they see the Lord who bore wounds on their account, but the righteous He brings into His glories, and they enjoy what the wicked cannot behold!

entries.section: 1. The sanctification of the land and its inhabitants:

paragraphs.text: 1 "In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. 2 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land. 3 And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth. 4 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive: 5 But he shall say, I am no prophet, I am an husbandman; for a man hath possessed me from my youth. 6 And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends."

He speaks of the mystery of the sanctification of the land (the body) and its inhabitants (the soul) through the fountain of the divine Blood, which cleanses from every sin and uncleanness, removes from us every unclean spirit, and destroys in us everything that is not of God, saying: "In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land" [1-2].

What is this fountain opened for us, the house of David, since we have become kings in it, and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that is, those who enjoy the vision of peace, which takes away sin and uncleanness, if not the wounds of the Lord Jesus?! It is the fountain of cleansing for us and at the same time the cause of judgment for the wicked. This is the fountain that never runs dry, so the Church continues to drink from it all the days of her life and is sanctified in it continually.

St. Didymus the Blind comments on this fountain, saying: [This sprinkling or pouring out is accomplished by the divine Blood of the Savior, of which St. Peter speaks... "Unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied"... as he says: "Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver or gold... But with the precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot" (1 Pet 1:18-19). Those who thus submit to the shed Blood receive a clean heart, saying, as though they were one person, in their repeated prayers without ceasing: "Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow," that they may obtain the purity of which it was said: "Pure religion and undefiled"].

This is our living fountain in which we are washed and cleansed from every uncleanness, and through it the names of the idols are cut off from the land, that everything belonging to the devil may be removed from the land of our body, so that it is no longer the land of his kingdom. If the Law forbade pronouncing the names of the pagan gods, it was so that no stranger should be remembered in our body, but God alone should reign over it. Sanctification does not stop at removing the names of the idols but extends to removing the false prophets who work on their behalf, and also removing the unclean spirit, which is the spirit of error and falsehood.

entries.section: 1. The sanctification of the land and its inhabitants:

paragraphs.text: The power of the holy life appears in his saying that when the godly parents mourn for their sins they do not leave their son to play the part of a false prophet, preferring to pierce their son with a spear so that he dies rather than allow him the false prophecy [3]. Thus through the holy life evil is removed completely and the false prophets are exposed and put to shame, and they do not wear a rough garment to deceive [4], so they do not wear the austere garb of the prophets, but deny that they are prophets. Thus God pours out upon His people the spirit of grace and sanctification, so that they are not deceived by false appearances and do not tolerate error.

entries.section: 1. The sanctification of the land and its inhabitants:

paragraphs.text: If anyone asks them about their wounds, since the prophets of the idols, especially of Baal, were known to cut themselves when they inquired of the gods (1 Kgs 18:28), each one of them answers out of fear and shame that he is not a prophet but merely a farmer who was wounded in the house of his friends and not in worship [5-6].

It is wonderful that while the false prophet in his deceit hides the real cause of his wounds, hiding that he wounded himself in misleading worship, the Lord Christ, the true Word of God, was truly wounded in the house of His friends, for His disciple betrayed Him and His own delivered Him to death... as though God brings forth, even from the words of the wicked, a true prophecy concerning what was to be accomplished in the person of the Messiah.

entries.section: 2. The wounded Shepherd:

paragraphs.text: 7 "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones. 8 And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the LORD, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. 9 And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The LORD is my God."

While the false prophet equivocates about his wounds, the Lord Christ announces His wounds beforehand in the spirit of prophecy, for it was said: "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones" [7].

St. John Chrysostom says: [Satan rages with great violence against the teachers, because by their destruction the flock is scattered. By slaughtering the sheep the flock is diminished, but by striking the shepherd the whole flock perishes... by one soul all perish]. This is what Satan thought he could do by striking the Messiah the Savior; he thought that by striking the Shepherd the sheep would be scattered, so that he might turn his hand and rule over the little ones]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Matthew the Evangelist wrote concerning this prophecy when Jesus was arrested and His disciples fled: "That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets" (Mt 2:23), "I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad" (Mt 26:31). It is understood from the word "smite" and other words concerning death that the Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep (Jn 10:15), gives His life a ransom for many (Mt 20:28)].

entries.section: 2. The wounded Shepherd:

paragraphs.text: Through these wounds the Lord says that two parts of the inhabitants of the earth "shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The LORD is my God" [8-9].

If, because of the rejection of the wounds of the Lord, or the rejection of the wounded Lord on behalf of mankind, two parts of the earth are cut off from the land of the living and die eternally, then the third part enters under the fire of affliction, to share with their wounded Savior in His wounds; or, in other words, they bear their wounds in them as a sign of their union with Him.

Through affliction the Church enters the furnace of the Cross, that the word of God may be proclaimed in her as silver purified seven times (Ps 12:6), and her life may be proclaimed as refined gold, that is, a heavenly, spiritual life full of true riches and eternal glory. If silver signifies the word of God, so every soul that desires to bear true silver, that is, a witness to the word of God, and to become of a heavenly nature (not earthly) and spiritual (not fleshly), possessing true riches and authority, is fitting to be tried by the fire of the Cross. Such a soul hears the divine voice saying: "It is my people," that is, He joins her to the true membership of His heavenly Church, while she sings joyfully to Him, saying: "The LORD is my God"!

entries.section: 1. The captivity of Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: "1 Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. 2 For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city." [1-2].

At the end of the previous chapter we saw that two parts of the earth are cut off and die, while the third remains in it, refined by fire like silver and tried like gold. As St. Didymus the Blind sees it, the two parts are the pagans and the Jews who reject salvation, while the third is the company of believers who were set free from the satanic captivity by the Cross and received the divine fire that gives sanctification, of which St. John the Baptist said: "He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire" (Mt 3:11), as the Lord Himself said: "I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?!" (Lk 12:49). St. Didymus the Blind sees that it is also the fire of trials that refines the soul, for he says: [Those who passed through the fire, that is, the last third of the captives who were purified and whose prayer the Lord answered, say to God who gave them peace: "For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried. Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins. Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place" (Ps 66:10-12). And in Isaiah also God the Savior of man says: "Fear not: for I am with thee. When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be scorched; neither shall the flame burn thee..." (Isa 43:3-4). How can there be walking in the fire and coming out of it without loss, unless we have the voice of the Lord, of whom it was said that He quenches the flame of the fire? For as the Red Sea was divided by the stroke of the holy rod and the people passed through without loss, so the flame of the fire is divided and opens for passage through it without burning].

The divine fire, whether the fire of the Holy Spirit who gives sanctification or the fire of the refining trials, increases the believer in radiance and glory, but the stubborn are shattered by it. Therefore he says: "Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee" [1]. The day of the Lord is a day of salvation for the submissive souls and their liberation from their captivity, but it is a harsh and bitter day for the arrogant souls that cling to their evil. As was said by the prophet Isaiah: "Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it" (Isa 13:9).

The spoils are usually divided outside the captured city, lest the captors be occupied with the booty and the captives recover their strength and fight them. But here he says: "Thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee," a sign of the enemies' contempt for the city and their realization that it is utterly shattered, with no possibility of her rising again. The hideousness of this contempt appears in their dividing the women among themselves as booty, to commit evil with them before their husbands, as was said by Isaiah: "Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished" (Isa 13:16).

St. Didymus the Blind sees that the divine wrath came upon Jerusalem to the uttermost (1 Thess 2:16) because of her killing of the Lord and His disciples, so she fell under the might of Justus the Roman commander, who destroyed her completely in a hideous manner recorded by Josephus the Jewish historian.

It is a painful picture of the soul that falls into the captivity of the devil through unbelief, so the enemy storms its depths and humiliates it within, and stirs up all the sins (the nations) against it, so he plunders every good thing in it and defiles the body (the women) with all its faculties, and every fruit (the children) is shattered.

entries.section: 1. The captivity of Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: It is wonderful that half of the city is carried into captivity outside, while the residue is not cut off from the city [2]. The first half signifies the old Jerusalem, or the Jews who reject the Savior, while the residue signifies those who accepted faith in Him, upon whom the Church, the new Jerusalem, was established. At the same time the first half signifies the old outer man who must be driven out, while the residue signifies the inner man who is renewed. May the old die and the new live in us!

entries.section: 2. On the Mount of Olives (the Lord bears our sufferings in us):

paragraphs.text: 3 Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. 4 And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south. 5 And ye shall flee to the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal: yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee.

As the old, literal, legal Jerusalem is shattered so that the new, spiritual Jerusalem may arise in us, that the Lord may dwell in her and fight for her and support her, revealing His Cross in her, he says: "Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south. And ye shall flee to the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal: yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee" [3-5].

Since man fell under the captivity of the devil and collapsed before the sins (the nations), his Creator came forward to set him free, for it was said: "Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle" [3]. The Lord Himself came forward to fight the devil with all his evils, to free man from his power. St. Didymus the Blind comments on the word "go forth," saying: [Yes, our Lord and Savior says of Himself in the Gospel: "For I proceeded forth and came from God (the Father); neither came I of myself, but he sent me" (Jn 8:42). In the same sense Habakkuk says to God: "Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, for the salvation of thine anointed; thou crushedst the head of the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation unto the neck" (Hab 3:13). And as He goes forth and comes to those whom He saves, so He goes forth more clearly when He makes war (against the devil). It is written in the book of Micah: "For, behold, the LORD cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth" (Mic 1:13), and in Isaiah: The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies" (Isa 42:13)].

The Lord goes forth to fight for us, and stands in that day, the day of redemption, upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mountain cleaves in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west to make a very great valley, and half of the mountain removes toward the north and half of it toward the south... What does this mean?

First: The Savior stood upon the mount of Olives east of Jerusalem as the Sower who planted the holy olive trees of which it was said: "But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God" (Ps 52:9), "thy children like olive plants round about thy table" (Ps 128:3). These trees, as St. Didymus says: [are not planted in the valley on the west, but on the mountain on high toward the east, and the Sun of Righteousness shines upon them with His divine light, as though they were the trees that the Lord planted in Paradise, in the garden of Eden eastward (Gen 2:8). Each of them hears the voice of the Crucified: "To day shalt thou be with me in paradise" (Lk 23:43), so the holy trees say with the Apostle: "But our conversation is in heaven" (Phil 3:20)].

Second: If we have been planted by Christ Jesus the Crucified as olive trees in the house of God east of Jerusalem, then we stand there with the disciples, contemplating the ascension of the Lord at the mount of Olives, awaiting His coming as the angel said (Acts 1:12).

entries.section: 2. On the Mount of Olives (the Lord bears our sufferings in us):

paragraphs.text: Third: By faith we were planted east of Jerusalem on the holy mountain, but the Jews, by their denial of the Messiah the Savior, descended into the very great valley toward the west [4], and with them all who deny the divine grace, and the valley is like the chasm that separates those planted in the east from those in the west.

Fourth: Half of the mountain removes toward the north, where the cold north wind is, and the other half toward the south, where the warm, hot wind is. The first half signifies the coldness of the spirit, or evil, and the other signifies the heat of the Spirit (the spiritual noonday). St. Didymus sees, in the words of the bride: "Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits" (Song 4:16), that the north wind signifies the devil, where the bitter cold destroys the crop and hinders the breezes of the divine fragrance, while the south wind, by its heat and its fragrance, inflames the soul, representing the Lord the Savior, who said: "I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?!" (Lk 12:49).

Let us say to the north wind, not with the tongue but with deeds, that it turn away far from us by fulfilling the words of the Apostle: "Abstain from all appearance of evil" (1 Thess 5:22), and let us call the south wind by receiving the Lord Christ in our life in practice!

entries.section: 2. On the Mount of Olives (the Lord bears our sufferings in us):

paragraphs.text: Fifth: St. Didymus sees, in the saying: "the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal" [5], that the ravine between the mountains reaches to Asahel, of whom it was said: "light of foot as a wild roe" (2 Sam 2:18). The believer in Christ Jesus runs among the holy mountains with light, swift feet toward his Bridegroom, with piercing spiritual glances toward Him.

Sixth: He says: "Yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee" [5]. This famous earthquake is the one that happened in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, and Amos mentioned it (Amos 1:1). And when Uzziah knew his sin toward the holy things by burning incense on the altar of incense (2 Chr 26:16), he was struck with leprosy in his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD and was driven out from there, and his son was set up in his place. So fleeing from the earthquake means our fleeing from what befell Uzziah, from the leprosy of his sin, that we may enjoy the indwelling of the Lord our God in us, that He may reign within us.

Let us flee from the earthquake of Uzziah to receive the earthquake of the Cross, through which many of the dead went into Jerusalem and appeared to many (Mt 27:51-52), that it may shake our earthly, dusty mind and raise up in us the living, spiritual mind.

entries.section: 3. The Cross as a known day:

paragraphs.text: 6 And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall be no light. The luminaries shall be drawn in. 7 But it shall be one day which shall be known to the LORD, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light. [6-7].

For as he speaks of the Cross in our life, he separates the trees planted in the east from those in the west, and those that receive the south wind from those that receive the north wind, and those that carry the Cross, hastening to Asahel with light feet and piercing sight toward their crucified Bridegroom, from the denying soul, and those that reject the earthquake of Uzziah from those that bow down to it... All this is fulfilled in the day of the Cross, which he described thus:
First: "There shall be no light," for darkness fell at the time of the Cross, revealing the authority that was given to darkness, but only for a time.
Second: "One day which shall be known to the LORD," and as St. Didymus says: [The day of the Lord is continuous, no night cuts it off]; it is the day of eternal light (Isa 60:9).

entries.section: 3. The Cross as a known day:

paragraphs.text: Third: "Not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light" [7]. It is not day because darkness covered the earth, nor is it night because it was the time of day; it is neither day nor night, but at evening time there is light, for the outer darkness was dispelled after the ninth hour, as the inner darkness was dispelled through the work of the Cross in the life of mankind.

entries.section: 4. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the Church:

paragraphs.text: 8 And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea: in summer and in autumn shall it be. 9 And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall the LORD be alone, and his name alone. 10 All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem: and it shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place, from Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses. 11 And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.

"And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea: in summer and in autumn shall it be" [8]. What are these waters but the waters of the Holy Spirit, which are bound to the Cross?! In our study of the Book of Ezekiel (Ezek 47) the waters were bound to the altar, that is, to the sacrifice of the Cross. And now, as he speaks of the Cross as a known day that occupies the mind of God, the springs of the Holy Spirit burst forth, going out from Jerusalem, where the Apostles were, to the eastern sea and the western sea, that is, to the Gentiles in the east and the west. In the Septuagint it came: "the former sea and the latter sea," that is, to work in the life of the Jews who came first and enjoyed the Law and then in the life of the Gentiles. Thus the door was opened by the outpouring upon all mankind, as the Lord said: "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28), and by this the name of God is glorified in all.

St. Didymus sees that these living waters that go out from Jerusalem to pour into the eastern and western seas are the spiritual Law, or divine knowledge, or divine love, things that overflow in the Church, the Jerusalem above, to work in the world for its sanctification, for he says: [This idea has crystallized from our interpretation: "They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea" (Isa 11:9); it is filled with the divine love that is from God, which overflows upon the chosen and covers a multitude of sins (Jas 5:20), covering the evil deeds so that nothing of them remains; so the knowledge of the Lord is water that covers the sea and turns it into sweet and pure waters].

We may say that our souls have become an eastern sea struck by self-righteousness (the blow from the right), or a western sea struck by the blows from the left; so we are in need of the work of the Holy Spirit in us to remove from us the salinity of our own waters and the salinity of the waters of evil, into the sweetness of the holy river that makes glad the city of God.

entries.section: 4. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the Church:

paragraphs.text: Through these new, sweet waters, that is, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, God reigns over the Church spread throughout the world, for he says: "And the LORD shall be king over the earth: in that day shall the LORD be alone, and his name alone" [9]... He reigns not over the Jews alone but also over the Gentiles who come to the Lord. And as St. Didymus says: [Formerly there was a difference between the eastern and western seas, that is, between the Jews and the Greeks. Not all acknowledge the oneness of God, for the pagans believe in many gods, while the Jews have one God; but when the Gospel came, the knowledge of the one and only Creator spread among all. Paul writes: "Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision by faith" (Rom 3:29)... The Lord shall be alone in that day which the LORD hath made (Ps 118:24), when the Sun of Righteousness arises (Mal 4:2), and His name alone also, for when all mankind are united in thought and blameless godliness they will have one name that points to God. By this the saying of the Psalm is fulfilled: "How wonderful is thy holy name in all the earth!" (Ps 8:1), and also: "Thou hast magnified thy holy name upon the earth" (Ps 137:2)... and by this the petition offered to God is fulfilled: "Hallowed be thy name"]...

entries.section: 4. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the Church:

paragraphs.text: The prophet continues his speech, saying: "All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem: and it shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place, from Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses. And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited" [10-11].

By these phrases he reveals the dimensions of the Church in which the Holy Spirit works as living waters flowing through the Cross, that the name of God alone may be glorified on the earth, and they can be summarized as follows:

First: He says: "All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem." Since "Geba" in St. Didymus' view means "testimony," and "Rimmon" means "a high or lofty place," in his opinion the dimensions of the knowledge of the Lord with which the Church overflows are the testimony to the Lord by the high (heavenly) Spirit. We may say that the Church in which the waters of the Holy Spirit overflow extends in the life of mankind from Geba, that is, from testimony to God in Christ Jesus, as the righteousness of God working in us, to bring us to Rimmon, that is, to lead us into the exalted, lofty life. As for Rimmon being south of Jerusalem, as we saw before, the south wind is hot and inflames our Jerusalem with the Spirit who neither cools nor grows lukewarm.

Second: "It shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place" [10].
