Since the soul is lifted up to Rimmon, it is fitting that we should not cease to be lifted up, and as St. Didymus says: [It carries a power from on high to be lifted up and not to descend, for it is fitting for those who have reached the goal and arrived at perfection itself through striving to stand firm in holiness].

Third: "From Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate" [10]. The living Church sets out from Benjamin's gate, that is, the gate of the son of the right hand, so she is like her Bridegroom who sits at the right hand of the Majesty; she has no members on the left, but all are sons of the right hand, that is, heirs of glory. The Church goes forth to the corner gate, so she is like the Lord, the cornerstone which the builders rejected (Ps 118:22; Isa 28:16; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:6), and He joined the Jews with the Gentiles in one integrated building. So the Church, like her Bridegroom, binds all together by the Holy Spirit to be one holy sanctuary to the Lord.

Therefore, let us enter by Benjamin's gate, which is called "the first gate," which none enters but he who is hidden in the Lord Christ, who says with boldness and power: "Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the LORD" (Ps 118:19), "This gate of the LORD, into which the righteous shall enter" (Ps 118:20). Let us enter this gate and be joined to the cornerstone, rejected by men and glorified by God, and let us not be like the hypocrites, who do not enter the heavenly gate but stand in the corners making long prayers to seek the praise of men.

Fourth: "From the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses" [10]. The word "Hananeel" in Hebrew means "God has been gracious" or "has shown favor"; it is a tower near the Sheep Gate and the tower of Meah as renewed by Nehemiah (Neh 3:1; 12:39). And the king's winepresses signify the spiritual house of wine (Song 2:4), which symbolizes inward joy. So the Church of the New Testament is characterized by the tower of "the free grace of God," of which the Lord spoke to His disciples, saying: "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him" (Lk 14:28-29). Thus a man begins his life in the Church by counting the cost: Does he have faith in the free grace of God? Can he enjoy the surpassing divine tower so that he may be fortified in it, saying: "For thou hast been a refuge for me, and a strong tower from the enemy. I will abide in thy tabernacle for ever: I will trust in the covert of thy wings" (Ps 61:3-4). Through this tower the believer goes forth to the king's winepresses, that is, to the house of wine, to be pressed with the Lord who passed through the winepress, to enjoy the joy of the Holy Spirit!

entries.section: 4. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the Church:

paragraphs.text: Fifth: "And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited" [11]. In place of the desolation that befell the soul because of sin, she is filled with glory and life, so she is inhabited not only by people but by God Himself, who sanctifies her, so she is enlarged with love for all mankind, and thus she comes out of the state of gloomy desolation to the state of fullness with the grace of God and love of neighbor and the sense of surpassing peace and inner security.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: 12 And this shall be the plague wherewith the LORD will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. 13 And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour. 14 And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance. 15 And so shall be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in these tents, as this plague. 16 And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. 17 And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain. 18 And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain; there shall be the plague, wherewith the LORD will smite the nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles. 19 This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles. 20 In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, "HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD"; and the pots in the LORD'S house shall be like the bowls before the altar. 21 Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the LORD of hosts: and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts.

The prophet concludes his speech about the saving work of God in His holy Church, whose dimensions we have seen, by revealing the necessity of pulling down the old man with all his evil works and the rising of the new man, holy in the Lord, declaring the following:

First: He declares the plague that strikes the pagan nations that surrounded Jerusalem to fight her, as a symbol of the works of the old man or the warfare of the sins, and he says: "Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth" [12]. If the body, before its sanctification, with its evil lusts represents the old man, then this body that carries enmity against God (Rom 8:7) melts away. And lest anyone think that the body in itself is evil, he said: "Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet," for what befalls the body is not the dissolution of its material being but of its old lusts, that it may bear sanctification in it; and so also their eyes consume away in their holes, that is, they are loosed from their old glances to receive a new inner spiritual insight that befits the new man, and their tongue consumes away in their mouth, so the tongue is not destroyed in itself but dies to its evil to offer a holy voice befitting the new life. So the destruction does not touch the body and its members in themselves but strikes the evil hidden in them, that blessing and righteousness may take its place.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Second: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour" [13]. St. Didymus explains the tumult here not as the loss of peace but as the sense of great wonder before the work of God, which bewilders the soul and makes it unable to comprehend His mysteries, as in the saying: "shall fear the LORD and his goodness in the latter days" (Hos 3:5), or "I have heard thy speech, and was afraid" (Hab 3:2). So every soul marvels before the work of God, and the man takes hold of the hand of his neighbor, so all walk together in one spirit in their spiritual striving.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Third: "And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance" [14]. Who is this Judah who fights at Jerusalem and not against Jerusalem, to gather on her behalf the wealth of the nations, gold and silver and abundant apparel, but the person of the Lord Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah, that is, the true Judah, dwelling in our inner Jerusalem, who fights the spiritual war for us as long as He dwells in us, to seize as booty for Himself the abilities and energies that were formerly used for evil, and to use them for our spiritual edification?! He is the true King who fights in the soul to give her victory and riches, so that she is adorned for Him as a heavenly queen?

If gold signifies the spirit or heaven, and silver speech or the divine word, and apparel the gifts, then our Bridegroom who dwells in us fights against the devil for the sanctification of our spirit and our mind and all our gifts.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Fourth: "And so shall be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in these tents, as this plague" [15].

St. Didymus sees that these animals signify the sins that the Spirit strikes, that is, the sins of the old man that must be abandoned. In his opinion the horse signifies a man's desire for his brother's wife, as the Scripture says: "They were as fed horses roaming at large; every one neighed after his neighbour's wife" (Jer 5:8). The mules signify the barrenness of the spirit, especially of those who practice virginity of the body without enjoying the virginity and purity of the spirit, so a man is like a eunuch not for the sake of the Kingdom but for the sake of people's admiration of them (Mt 19:12). The camels signify those who care for God's law but without discernment, for they do not have the cloven hoof, so they are unclean (Lev 11:14). The asses signify lack of understanding; they are weighed down with burdens, their heads bowed toward the earth, unable to look toward the Jerusalem above.
Thus by the Holy Spirit the plague strikes these evil works under whose yoke man fell, until he is freed from them.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Fifth: He tells us of the Gentiles' enjoyment of the feast of tabernacles, for they go up to Jerusalem from year to year to worship the great King [16-19]. Not the Jews alone keep the feast, but the Gentiles enjoy this feast, where the Church of the New Testament sets out toward the heavenly Jerusalem without ceasing to sanctify the world, so men keep the feast of tabernacles, realizing that their bodies, the "tabernacles," have been sanctified to the Lord, and through them they worship the King, the LORD of hosts, until they put them off (2 Pet 1:14) to put them on again as spiritual bodies on the great day. They are the very same bodies but bear a nature befitting eternity. In this the Apostle Paul speaks to us, declaring how the believer longs not to put off the body but to bear it anew, so that death can no longer prevail over it, for he says: "For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life" (2 Cor 4:5).

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Sixth: He returns to affirm the sanctification of the body by saying that upon the bells of the horses is written "Holiness unto the LORD" [20]. If the horses signify the body, then even its bells become holiness unto the Lord, meaning that there is not in the body an unclean member or an impure sense, but everything in it, within and without, is holiness unto the Lord.

entries.section: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

paragraphs.text: Once again he affirms the holiness of everything on behalf of the Lord, saying that the pots that are in the Lord's house and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah shall be "holiness unto the LORD of hosts" [21], as though there is nothing defiled or unclean in the holy Church, but everything is like a pot or vessel that holds within it the heavenly treasure.

For the last time he affirms the same meaning by saying: "There shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts" [21], that is, there is no opponent of God and no idol worshiper within the true Church, and nothing strange within the true believer.
